```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(ggplot2); library(chanwer) })
chanwe_load_fonts()
set.seed(11)
L <- function(eb, t, s, src) labs(title = chanwe_title(t, eyebrow = eb), subtitle = s, caption = paste("Fuente ·", src))
prov <- c("Mendoza", "Córdoba", "Santa Fe", "Buenos Aires", "Tucumán", "Salta", "Neuquén", "Chubut", "Misiones", "Entre Ríos")
months <- seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 60)
unemp <- data.frame(date = months, value = 9 + cumsum(rnorm(60, 0, .25)) + 2.5 * plogis((seq_along(months) - 38) / 2))
cn <- c("Argentina", "Brasil", "Chile", "Uruguay", "Paraguay", "Perú", "Bolivia", "Colombia")
act <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(cn), function(i) data.frame(date = months, country = cn[i],
  value = 100 + cumsum(rnorm(60, c(.15, .35, .45, .3, .25, .4, .2, .3)[i], .9)))))
act$country <- factor(act$country, cn)
regions <- data.frame(region = c("Cuyo", "Pampeana", "NOA", "Patagonia", "NEA"), value = c(41.2, 33.8, 27.5, 22.9, 18.4))
weeks <- expand.grid(week = 1:12, region = c("Norte", "Centro", "Oeste", "Sur")); weeks$delta <- round(rnorm(48, 0, 4.5), 1)
mt <- mtcars; mt$tr <- factor(ifelse(mt$am == 1, "Manual", "Automática"), c("Manual", "Automática"))
```

# The grammar

Every chart in this catalogue follows the CHANWE v2 chart grammar (the brand
hub's `plot` tokens). These are the rules the last part of the document checks
the other plots against.

- **One orange signal.** The series, bar or group that matters is orange; the
  rest sit on the slate ramp. The categorical eight only when nothing is the
  point, in their fixed order.
- **Quiet names.** Axis labels and series names are visible but never the
  protagonist: slate mono, never the series colour (Ale, 2026-11-19).
- **Grid and marks.** Horizontal hairlines only, no axis lines or ticks; lines
  at 2px, rounded bars, points only where they mean something.
- **Colour never alone.** Every series is named; status colours (green, red)
  appear as dots, pills, pastel steps or signed values, never as a wash; orange
  is never the background of an area (a fading gradient carries it lightly).
- **The header.** An eyebrow for the topic, a title that states the claim, a
  subtitle with the metric, the unit and the period; the source in the footer.
- **Numbers in Spanish.** Decimal comma, a space before `%`, months as
  `jun-25`.

# The everyday charts

The five builders of round 6. Each returns a ggplot with the Chanwe theme; add
`labs()` for the title, the subtitle and the source. The first style is the
default.

## The header

`theme_chanwe()` keeps today's band (its text now white); `eyebrow_style =
"dot"` is the brand eyebrow without the band.

```{r}
#| label: hdr
#| layout-ncol: 1
d4 <- act[act$country %in% cn[1:4] & act$date >= as.Date("2024-01-01"), ]
hl <- L("Actividad · Región", "Actividad económica", "Índice, 2016 = 100, mensual, ene-24 a dic-25", "INDEC")
chanwe_lines(d4, "date", "value", "country") + hl
chanwe_lines(d4, "date", "value", "country", theme = theme_chanwe(eyebrow_style = "dot")) + hl
```

## Bars

`chanwe_bars(style = "labelled")` (default), `"ranking"` and `"lollipop"`.

```{r}
#| label: bars
bl <- L("Ventas · Región", "Cuyo lidera las ventas", "USD millones, acumulado ene-dic 2025", "elaboración propia")
chanwe_bars(regions, "region", "value") + bl
chanwe_bars(regions, "region", "value", style = "ranking", reference = median(regions$value)) + bl
chanwe_bars(regions, "region", "value", style = "lollipop") + bl
```

## Several series

`chanwe_lines(style = "direct")` (default) and `"spaghetti"`.

```{r}
#| label: lines
ll <- L("Actividad · Región", "Argentina crece por debajo de sus vecinos", "Índice, 2016 = 100, mensual, ene-21 a dic-25", "INDEC, bancos centrales")
chanwe_lines(act[act$country %in% cn[1:4], ], "date", "value", "country") + ll
chanwe_lines(act, "date", "value", "country", style = "spaghetti") + ll
```

## Area

`chanwe_area()`: the line over a gradient that fades to the axis.

```{r}
#| label: area
chanwe_area(unemp, "date", "value") + L("Empleo", "El desempleo sube desde 2024", "Personas desocupadas, millones, mensual, ene-21 a dic-25", "INDEC")
```

## Diverging heatmap

`chanwe_heatmap()` (today's tiles) and `labels = TRUE`.

```{r}
#| label: heat
hm <- L("Desvío · Plan", "Desvío semanal contra el plan", "Puntos porcentuales, semanas 1 a 12 de 2026", "elaboración propia")
chanwe_heatmap(weeks, "week", "region", "delta") + hm
chanwe_heatmap(weeks, "week", "region", "delta", labels = TRUE) + hm
```

## Distributions

`chanwe_density(style = "gradient")` (default) and `"outline"`.

```{r}
#| label: dens
dl <- L("Consumo", "Los manuales rinden más", "Densidad de millas por galón, 32 modelos, 1974", "Motor Trend, 1974")
chanwe_density(mt, "mpg", "tr") + dl
chanwe_density(mt, "mpg", "tr", style = "outline") + dl
```

# The catalogue

The builders of rounds 7 and 8.

## Dot plot

```{r}
#| label: dots
dp <- data.frame(p = prov, v = round(runif(10, 18, 46), 1)); dp$lo <- dp$v - runif(10, 2, 6); dp$hi <- dp$v + runif(10, 2, 6)
dpl <- L("Empleo · Provincias", "Mendoza, cuarta en informalidad", "Asalariados sin descuento jubilatorio, %, 3.er trimestre 2025", "EPH, INDEC")
chanwe_dots(dp, "p", "v", focus = "Mendoza") + dpl
chanwe_dots(dp, "p", "v", focus = "Mendoza", style = "range", lo = "lo", hi = "hi") + dpl
```

## Dumbbell and slope

```{r}
#| label: dumbbell-slope
db <- data.frame(p = prov[1:8], a = round(runif(8, 20, 40), 1)); db$b <- db$a + round(rnorm(8, 3, 4), 1)
chanwe_dumbbell(db, "p", "a", "b", labels = c("2024", "2025")) +
  L("Pobreza · Provincias", "La pobreza cambió poco", "Personas pobres, %, 1.er semestre 2024 y 2025", "EPH, INDEC")
sl <- data.frame(p = prov[1:7], a = round(runif(7, 10, 30), 1)); sl$b <- sl$a + round(rnorm(7, 1, 5), 1)
chanwe_slope(sl, "p", "a", "b", labels = c("2020", "2025"), focus = "Mendoza") +
  L("Exportaciones · Provincias", "Mendoza ganó terreno", "Participación en las exportaciones regionales, %, 2020 y 2025", "INDEC")
```

## Scatter

```{r}
#| label: scatter
sc <- data.frame(p = c(prov, paste("Región", 1:14)), x = runif(24, 20, 60)); sc$y <- 8 + .45 * sc$x + rnorm(24, 0, 4); sc$pop <- runif(24, .3, 9)
scl <- L("Productividad", "Más inversión, más productividad", "Inversión por ocupado (USD miles) y productividad (índice), 2025", "elaboración propia")
ax <- labs(x = "Inversión por ocupado", y = "Productividad")
chanwe_scatter(sc, "x", "y", "p", focus = "Mendoza", highlight = c("Córdoba", "Neuquén")) + ax + scl
chanwe_scatter(sc, "x", "y", "p", focus = "Mendoza", style = "trend") + ax + scl
chanwe_scatter(sc, "x", "y", "p", focus = "Mendoza", style = "bubble", size = "pop") + ax + scl
```

## Waterfall

```{r}
#| label: waterfall
wf <- data.frame(k = c("2024", "Precios", "Volumen", "Mix", "Tipo de cambio", "Costos"), v = c(120, 18, 9, -4, -14, -7))
wfl <- L("Resultado", "Los precios explican casi todo el aumento", "Resultado operativo, USD millones, 2024 a 2025", "estados contables")
chanwe_waterfall(wf, "k", "v", end_label = "2025") + wfl
chanwe_waterfall(wf, "k", "v", end_label = "2025", style = "totals") + wfl
```

## Composition over time

```{r}
#| label: stack
st <- expand.grid(y = 2021:2025, s = c("Energía", "Agro", "Industria", "Servicios"))
st$v <- c(18, 22, 25, 31, 38, 30, 29, 33, 31, 34, 22, 21, 20, 19, 18, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17)
stl <- L("Exportaciones · Sectores", "La energía ya es la primera exportación", "Exportaciones de Mendoza por sector, USD millones", "INDEC")
chanwe_stack(st, "y", "s", "v") + stl
chanwe_stack(st, "y", "s", "v", style = "share") + stl + labs(subtitle = "Participación por sector, % del total")
chanwe_stack(st, "y", "s", "v", style = "grouped", compare = c("2021", "2025")) + stl + labs(subtitle = "USD millones, 2021 y 2025")
```

## Histogram and spread

```{r}
#| label: hist-spread
hv <- data.frame(v = rlnorm(900, 6.4, .45))
hl2 <- L("Ingresos", "La mitad gana menos de 600 mil", "Ingreso mensual por ocupado, miles de pesos, 3.er trimestre 2025", "EPH, INDEC")
chanwe_histogram(hv, "v") + hl2
chanwe_histogram(hv, "v", style = "split", note = "← La mitad que gana menos") + hl2
bx <- data.frame(r = rep(c("Cuyo", "Pampeana", "NOA", "Patagonia", "NEA"), each = 60))
bx$v <- rlnorm(300, rep(c(6.3, 6.5, 6.1, 6.7, 6.0), each = 60), .35)
bxl <- L("Ingresos · Regiones", "Patagonia paga más y más parejo", "Ingreso mensual por ocupado, miles de pesos, 3.er trimestre 2025", "EPH, INDEC")
chanwe_spread(bx, "r", "v", focus = "Cuyo") + bxl
chanwe_spread(bx, "r", "v", focus = "Cuyo", style = "violin") + bxl
```

## Ranking, multiples and progress

```{r}
#| label: bump-multiples-bullet
bp <- expand.grid(y = 2019:2025, p = prov[1:7])
bp$score <- rnorm(nrow(bp), 0, .35) + rep(seq(1.2, -1.2, length.out = 7), each = 7) + as.numeric(bp$p == "Mendoza") * ((bp$y - 2019) * .55 - 1.6)
bp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(bp, bp$y), function(g) transform(g, rk = rank(-score))))
chanwe_bump(bp, "y", "p", "rk", focus = "Mendoza") +
  L("Competitividad", "Mendoza subió al primer puesto", "Ranking provincial de competitividad, 2019 a 2025", "elaboración propia")
mm <- expand.grid(t = 1:36, p = prov[1:6]); mm$v <- ave(rnorm(nrow(mm), .3, 1), mm$p, FUN = cumsum)
chanwe_multiples(mm, "t", "v", "p") + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
  L("Empleo · Provincias", "Seis provincias, seis caminos", "Empleo registrado, variación acumulada en puntos, ene-23 a dic-25", "SIPA")
bt <- data.frame(k = c("Ventas", "Margen", "Clientes nuevos", "Retención", "NPS"), a = c(82, 64, 91, 77, 58), t = c(90, 70, 85, 80, 65))
chanwe_bullet(bt, "k", "a", "t") +
  L("Metas · 2025", "Cuatro de cinco metas, todavía lejos", "Avance contra la meta anual, %, a noviembre de 2025", "tablero de gestión")
```

## Part of a whole

`chanwe_whole(style = "bar")` (default), `"donut"`, `"waffle"` and `"treemap"`.

```{r}
#| label: whole
pw <- data.frame(k = c("Energía", "Agro", "Industria", "Servicios", "Turismo", "Otros"), v = c(34, 28, 16, 10, 7, 5))
pwl <- L("Exportaciones · Sectores", "La energía, un tercio de lo exportado", "Exportaciones de Mendoza por sector, %, 2025", "INDEC")
for (s in c("bar", "donut", "waffle", "treemap")) print(chanwe_whole(pw, "k", "v", style = s) + pwl)
```

## Forecast

`chanwe_forecast(style = "fan")` (default) and `"zone"`, its range a shaded
band.

```{r}
#| label: forecast
mo <- seq(as.Date("2023-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 48)
fv <- data.frame(d = mo, v = 2.6 + cumsum(c(rnorm(36, -.03, .22), rep(-.04, 12))), s = pmax(seq_len(48) - 36, 0) * .15)
fl <- L("Inflación", "La inflación seguiría bajando en 2026", "Variación mensual del IPC, %, ene-23 a dic-26; proyección desde ene-26", "INDEC, proyección propia")
chanwe_forecast(fv, "d", "v", from = mo[36], spread = "s") + fl
chanwe_forecast(fv, "d", "v", from = mo[36], spread = "s", style = "zone") + fl
```

## Level and change

`chanwe_level_change(style = "change")` (default), `"panels"` and `"strip"`;
never a second axis.

```{r}
#| label: level-change
cb <- data.frame(y = 2014:2025, v = c(700, 735, 690, 760, 820, 790, 640, 760, 880, 910, 870, 960))
cl <- L("Producción", "2025, récord de la serie", "Producción, miles de toneladas, y su variación anual, 2014 a 2025", "elaboración propia")
chanwe_level_change(cb, "y", "v") + cl
chanwe_level_change(cb, "y", "v", style = "panels", level_name = "Miles de toneladas") + cl
chanwe_level_change(cb, "y", "v", style = "strip") + cl
```

# Plots elsewhere, checked

```{r}
#| label: review-data
ext <- list.files("catalogue/external", pattern = "\\.jpg$")
src <- sub("--.*", "", ext)
sources <- c(`chanwer-pdf` = "chanwer, the PDF showcase", `chanwer-inst` = "chanwer, inst/examples scripts",
             `chanwer-readme` = "chanwer, README", `brand-html` = "chanwe-brand, HTML components starter",
             `brand-demo` = "chanwe-brand, brand demo example", `brand-gtgg` = "chanwe-brand, gt + ggplot example")
# One verdict per plot: (pattern, verdict, what is wrong, the builder that replaces it)
rules <- list(
  c("preview|display_color_palettes-0[1-4]|focus-palette", "Reference", "A palette swatch, not a chart.", "—"),
  c("form-area|showcase-chunk-16|fig-area", "Fails", "Orange (and blue) as the background of an area.", "chanwe_area() / chanwe_stack()"),
  c("form-density|showcase-chunk-13", "Fails", "Opaque or translucent fills cover each other; the overlap is hidden.", "chanwe_density()"),
  c("showcase-chunk-09|showcase-chunk-10|complex-box", "Fails", "Boxes and violins filled with the categorical hues: colour as a wash.", "chanwe_spread()"),
  c("showcase-chunk-11|simple-bar|cat-bars|ordinal|display_color_palettes-06", "Fails", "Bars in three or more saturated hues with no focus; no values.", "chanwe_bars() / chanwe_stack()"),
  c("div-heat|display_color_palettes-08", "Complies", "Today's heatmap, kept as the default by Ale; labels now optional.", "chanwe_heatmap()"),
  c("div-bars", "Partly", "Signed bars in green and red: allowed as signed values, but saturated and unlabelled.", "chanwe_bars() / chanwe_dots()"),
  c("frame-card|frame-editorial|v2-focus|kpi-valence|display_core_components-02|fig-margen|fig-disp|fig-barras-h|fig-ancha", "Complies", "One orange signal, slate context.", "—"),
  c("form-line|fig-linea|fig-tab", "Partly", "Focus right, but a legend or coloured names instead of quiet direct labels.", "chanwe_lines()"),
  c("fig-barras", "Partly", "Focus and slate right, but grouped bars without values.", "chanwe_stack(style = \"grouped\")"),
  c("seq-|form-errorbar|form-focus", "Partly", "Readable, but the colour encodes a third variable or the values are missing.", "chanwe_scatter() / chanwe_bars()"),
  c(".", "Partly", "Three categorical hues where a focus would carry the claim; a descriptive title.", "chanwe_scatter() / chanwe_lines()")
)
verdict <- t(vapply(ext, function(f) { for (r in rules) if (grepl(r[1], f)) return(r[2:4]); c("Partly", "", "") }, character(3)))
review <- data.frame(file = ext, source = src, verdict = verdict[, 1], issue = verdict[, 2], builder = verdict[, 3])
```

Every plot found outside the builders: `r nrow(review)` figures in six sources,
rendered as their documents render them today, each checked against the
grammar. *Complies* follows it; *Partly* is readable but misses a rule;
*Fails* breaks one of the grammar's hard rules (an orange or categorical wash,
hidden overlaps, hues with no focus); *Reference* is a palette swatch.

```{r}
#| label: review-summary
tab <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(factor(sources[review$source], sources), factor(review$verdict, c("Complies", "Partly", "Fails", "Reference"))))
tab <- data.frame(Source = rownames(tab), tab, row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE)
tab$Total <- rowSums(tab[, -1])
chanwe_kbl(tab, title = "Verdicts by source", stub = "Source", density = "compact",
           caption = "Fuente · this review, 85 figures rendered on 2026-11-19.")
```

```{r}
#| label: review-figures
#| results: asis
for (s in names(sources)) {
  r <- review[review$source == s, ]
  if (!nrow(r)) next
  cat("\n\n## ", sources[[s]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("::: {layout-ncol=2}\n\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(r))) {
    cat(sprintf("![**%s.** %s%s](catalogue/external/%s){width=100%%}\n\n", r$verdict[i], r$issue[i],
                if (r$builder[i] %in% c("", "—")) "" else paste0(" Use `", r$builder[i], "`."), r$file[i]))
  }
  cat(":::\n\n")
}
```

# Findings

- **The everyday chart forms in the showcases and the brand examples still
  carry the pre-v2 look**: categorical hues where a focus would carry the
  claim, solid orange and blue areas, overlapping density fills and
  colour-filled boxes and violins. Each now has a builder that replaces it.
- **The chanwe-brand examples** (the brand demo, the gt + ggplot example and the
  HTML starter's charts) should be rewritten with the builders: they are the
  pages people copy from.
- **The README's second example does not run** (it uses a `sales` data frame it
  never defines), so it is not copy-pasteable as `AGENTS.md` asks.
- **Two scripts in `inst/examples` are developer diagnostics**
  (`kpi_layout_map.R`, `reproduce_chanwe_outputs.R`) that draw nothing to keep;
  `display_color_palettes.R` and `display_core_components.R` still run.
- **What already complies**: the figure frame (`chanwe_figure()`, card and
  editorial), the v2 focus charts, the KPI chart and the HTML starter's
  single-series and ranking charts.
